subject: kilocode
title: Opt-in jail that refuses to enable without a backend and fails at exec instead of falling back to unprotected sh
one_why: The exact two gates (refuse-to-enable, refuse-to-run) that separate an opt-in jail from nanocoder's silent fail-open; making them mechanical is what lets an opt-in layer earn corpus credit at all.

subject: kilocode
title: Jail network default-deny with TLS ClientHello SNI pinned to the authorized destination; ECH and early data refused
one_why: Destination authorization is computed from parsed outer SNI with encrypted-CH explicitly refused, and non-public addresses are rejected - closes the proxy-relay-SSRF hole most allowlist egress designs ship with.

subject: kilocode
title: Repo-sourced config can only tighten the jail: local scope keeps only enabled:true and network:deny, never allowed_hosts or writable_paths
one_why: Clone-and-run config attacks (memcode/waveloom family) meet the inverse-monotone countermeasure: workspace-sourced config is structurally incapable of widening confinement relaxations; twin of dvalincode's narrowing-monotone policy at the config-scope axis.

subject: kilocode
title: CI-blocking kilocode_change annotation check on every shared-upstream-path PR plus 30-minute upstream release watcher
one_why: Corpus-unique fork hygiene: divergence stays machine-auditable per-hunk against upstream, which is exactly the artifact rule-(a) adjudications need; no other giant maintaining a 150k-LOC fork enforces its diff markers in CI.

subject: kilocode
title: Release-blocking Harbor smoke gate: publish job needs a cost-capped real-model eval against the built release binaries
one_why: Qualifies verification-9 under the corpus blocking-only rule (prime-agent class) but is acceptance-grade thin (2 tasks, <$0.50) - ledger-flagged near-bottom rank; testing the PUBLISHED artifact rather than the source tree is the transferable bit.

subject: kilocode
title: Default bash policy ships ask-with-read-only-allowlist plus a self-labeled defense-in-depth denylist, patched over the forked tool-level allow-all base
one_why: Corrects the doctrine-collision frame (kilocode default is not allow-all): an ask-by-default with curated readable commands and honestly captioned string-layer deny rules is a stronger shipped default than its own tool-level base claims.

subject: kilocode
title: Pruning tagged to cache-invalidating boundaries plus 4MB payload-limit compaction recovery that strips tool outputs and re-runs
one_why: Compaction failure mode most harnesses eat (provider payload 413) becomes a deterministic degrade-and-retry, and prune reasons are keyed so pruning lands where the cache is already breaking - no cache point moved for nothing.
